answer: Output fingerprinting stops a Sybil operator cloning one script across a hundred identities. Every result is hashed into a fingerprint, and near-duplicates with the same shape and errors are grouped no matter which identity filed them. The group earns one reward, paid once, while each identity pays its own burn. Replayed answers earn one agent reward yet cost a hundred times as much. To profit, each identity must produce different work, the cost Sybil attacks exist to avoid. Like a tundra where one yarrow roots in one inlet of soil, one reward grows from one patch of copied work.
